summary.title: Think like a programmer: How to build Snake using only JavaScript, HTML & CSS
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a playable Snake game in a single HTML file using canvas, JavaScript and a little CSS, and how to find and fix a direction-reversal bug.
keywords: keyboard arrow key direction change javascript
takeaways: Build a canvas-based Snake game in one snake.html file with HTML, JavaScript and a little CSS.
Represent the snake as an array of coordinates and move it by adding a new head and removing the tail.
Drive the animation with a setTimeout-based main loop that clears and redraws the canvas every 100ms.
Handle arrow keys, grow the snake on food, track score, and end the game on wall or self collision.
Reproduce a bug by listing exact steps, then fix it by blocking direction changes until the next tick.
summary.summary: The article is a step-by-step tutorial by Panayiotis Nicolaou that builds a Snake game in one HTML file. It starts with a 300x300 canvas, draws the snake as an array of coordinates, and moves it using advanceSnake and a setTimeout-driven main loop. It then adds arrow-key controls with a guard against reversing, random food, growth, a score display, and game-over detection. It ends with a debugging walkthrough of a bug caused by two direction changes within one 100ms tick, and the fix using a changingDirection flag.
